---
title: "Getting Started"
guide-section: "Start Here"
---

Ten minutes, no cloud account: a local Icechunk repository and a directory of
files, registered in a fresh repository, committed, changed on a branch, and
landed. Every command below was run as shown; ids will differ on your machine.

## Install

```bash
pip install "tether-vcs[cli,icechunk]"      # what this page needs
pip install "tether-vcs[cli,icechunk,neon]"  # add the backends you use
pip install "tether-vcs[all]"                # everything
```

The distribution is `tether-vcs` (PyPI reserves the bare name); the package
you import and the command you run are both `tether`. Python 3.11 or newer.

Extras per backend: `objectstore` (S3/GCS/Azure for `file`; `s3`, `gcs`,
`azure` are aliases), `icechunk`, `neon`, `iceberg`, `delta`, `lance`,
`lakefs`, `ducklake`, `dolt`.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
- `git` or `jj` on `PATH`. tether keeps its history in *your* repository, not
  its own.
- Remote objects (S3, Neon, a catalog) need credentials. They never go in the
  repository -- see [Configuration](08-configuration.qmd#trust-boundary-tethersecretstoml).
- Backends marked *experimental* in [Backends](09-backends.qmd) have run
  against a fake of the service, not the service itself.
:::

## Some data to track

Use anything you have, or make a small sample: an Icechunk repository with one
array, and a directory of three files.

```python
import pathlib, icechunk, zarr

data = pathlib.Path("data")
storage = icechunk.local_filesystem_storage(str(data / "imaging.icechunk"))
repo = icechunk.Repository.create(storage)
session = repo.writable_session("main")
root = zarr.create_group(store=session.store)
root.create_array("labels", shape=(4, 8, 8), chunks=(1, 8, 8), dtype="u1")[:] = 0
session.commit("plate1: empty labels")

raw = data / "raw" / "plate1"
raw.mkdir(parents=True)
for i in range(3):
    (raw / f"well_{i}.tif").write_bytes(bytes([i]) * 64)
```

## Register and commit

tether lives inside a git or jj repository. Make one next to the data:

```bash
jj git init my-dataset && cd my-dataset      # or: git init my-dataset
tether init
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk ../data/imaging.icechunk
tether add raw/plate1   --kind file     ../data/raw/plate1/
tether status
```

```
dataset 61d0206e8d81; on trunk bookmark main
        new  raw/plate1  [file/observed]
        new  zarr/imaging  [icechunk/forkable]
```

`init` and `add` wrote small TOML manifests under `.tether/` and put the
working copy on `main`, the dataset's *trunk*. `status` was the first command
to touch the data: it fingerprinted both objects (an Icechunk snapshot id, a
digest over the files). The bracket names each object's *tier* -- what
tether can do with it. Icechunk is *forkable*: it can be pinned and branched.
A directory is *observed*: tether can tell you it changed, nothing more.

```bash
tether commit -m "Baseline: plate1 imaging and raw files"
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.4e9503fc.73e341e966c83d38
  recorded raw/plate1 (not recoverable)
committed b55326ca55a0
```

One command did three things: created an Icechunk tag (the *pin*) holding the
snapshot, wrote both states into the manifests, and made a jj/git commit of
those manifests with the `main` bookmark on it. `b55326ca55a0` is now the
handle for this exact combination of states.

## Read it back

Any process can open an object *as it was* at a commit:

```bash
tether open zarr/imaging --rev b55326ca55a0
```

```
/path/to/data/imaging.icechunk#tether.4e9503fc.73e341e966c83d38
```

```python
from tether import Repo

repo = Repo.find(".")
h = repo.open("zarr/imaging", rev="b55326ca55a0")   # read-only IcechunkHandle at the tag
zarr.open_group(h.session.store, mode="r")
```

For a whole job, set `TETHER_REV=b55326ca55a0` and every `repo.open(key)` in
it resolves read-only at that commit's pins -- no code change. The directory
cannot be opened at a revision: its state is a digest, not an address, which
is what `not recoverable` meant above.

## Change it on a branch

A *bookmark* is a branch of the dataset and, with it, a branch in every
system that has them. Start one:

```bash
tether new -b relabel
```

```
on bookmark relabel; working refs set up
  zarr/imaging -> tether.ws.4e9503fc.relabel  (created on first writable open)
```

Nothing was written yet. The branch appears in the Icechunk repository the
first time you open the object writable, forked from the pin `main` holds:

```python
import zarr
from tether import Repo

repo = Repo.find(".")
h = repo.open("zarr/imaging")             # writable: this forks tether.ws.4e9503fc.relabel
group = zarr.open_group(h.session.store, mode="a")
group["labels"][:] = 1
h.session.commit("Relabel plate1")        # an Icechunk commit on the branch
```

`main` -- the bookmark and the Icechunk branch -- is untouched. Record the
result and compare it with the trunk:

```bash
tether commit -m "Relabel plate1"
tether diff main relabel --content
```

```
  pinned zarr/imaging -> tether.4e9503fc.89c7e63509153c4f
committed 7eb84262ce1b
```

```
    changed  zarr/imaging  [+0 -0 ~1 nodes]
               modified  /labels  4 chunks
```

`commit` pinned the branch head and moved the `relabel` bookmark onto the new
commit. Both commits stay readable: `open --rev b55326ca55a0` still gives the
zeros.

## Land it

`promote` makes each system's upstream branch point at what the bookmark
pinned, then moves the `main` bookmark to the commit. Every command that
writes to a store takes `--dry-run`, so look first:

```bash
tether promote --dry-run
```

```
plan: promote (1 write(s))
        fast-forward  zarr/imaging  [icechunk] main  main snapshot_id=SHS2X3EVBHMYV1BQ… -> snapshot_id=TY7E8S29CEP987JJ… (base unchanged since fork)
                      raw/plate1: not forkable; nothing to promote
```

```bash
tether promote
tether verify --all-history
```

```
  fast-forwarded zarr/imaging -> {'snapshot_id': 'TY7E8S29CEP987JJ1VX0'}
  skipped        raw/plate1
main -> 7eb84262ce1b
```

```
        ok  1609e5dbca9d:zarr/imaging
        ok  7eb84262ce1b:zarr/imaging
        ok  b55326ca55a0:zarr/imaging
```

Icechunk's `main` was fast-forwarded (nothing else had moved it since the
fork), `main` the bookmark now names the relabel commit, and `verify` confirms
every pin any commit ever made still resolves -- the check to put in CI.

## What was written

Everything committed is small, text, and reviewable in `jj diff` / `git diff`:
`tether.toml` (the dataset's id and config) and `.tether/objects/<key>.toml`
(one manifest per object: kind, locator, state, pin). Per-checkout files --
`.tether/workspace.toml` (which bookmark you are on, which branches you write
through) and `.tether/ops.jsonl` (what tether did to the stores, for `undo`)
-- are untracked. The full layout is in
[Configuration](08-configuration.qmd#layout).

## Next

Remote systems register the same way; only the locator changes:

```bash
tether add zarr/imaging --kind icechunk s3://bucket/imaging.icechunk
tether add db/metrics   --kind neon --project-id prj-123 --database neondb --role runner
tether add features     --kind lance s3://bucket/features.lance
tether add code         --kind git ../analysis-code
```
